# NOTES: *The Impostor* by Harold Bindloss (Ward, Lock & Co.; Gutenberg #39698)

Single novel, no BOOK headings. 26 chapters.

## Contents
I Rancher Witham; II Lance Courthorne; III Trooper Shannon's Quarrel; IV In the Bluff; V Miss Barrington Comes Home; VI Anticipations; VII Witham's Decision; VIII Witham Comes to Silverdale; IX An Armistice; X Maud Barrington's Promise; XI Speed the Plough; XII Mastery Recognized; XIII A Fair Advocate; XIV The Unexpected; XV Facing the Flame; XVI Maud Barrington is Merciless; XVII With the Stream; XVIII Under Test; XIX Courthorne Blunders; XX The Face at the Window; XXI Colonel Barrington is Convinced; XXII Sergeant Stimson Confirms his Suspicions; XXIII The Revelation; XXIV Courthorne makes Reparation; XXV Witham Rides Away; XXVI Reinstation.

(Frontispiece: "In the meanwhile, Maud Barrington sat by the open window in her room." Ch. XVI.)

## Characters
- **Rancher Witham** (Frederick "F." Witham; English-born, ~26, grey eyes, bronzed face, crisp fair hair, bronze moustache). Prairie farmer near Canadian settlement (unnamed in text; hotel run by father of **Nettie**, a hotel-keeper's daughter). Lost two harvests, stock killed in blizzard, mortgage to be foreclosed in August. Left England 8 years earlier; girl left behind sent back letters for a silver-printed card (6 years prior). Had a rifle marked "F. Witham." Horses: two broncos (one shot by Witham to end suffering). Drowned-presumed in river ice.
- **Lance Courthorne**: gambler, cattle-thief/whisky-runner, son of late **Geoffrey Courthorne** (disinherited him; Silverdale land recorded in Geoffrey's name). Cavalier-looking, blue eyes, languid, imperious voice, black horse. Killed Trooper Shannon. Hires Witham for $100 to ride his black horse as decoy. Later mother's name unspecified; knew Witham's mother ("Mrs. Witham"/Miss Barrington knew "your mother" as Witham's). Final: shot by Corporal Payne while fleeing; dies after deposition.
- **Trooper Shannon** (Irish, from Ontario bush; family Orange; sister-of-Larry-Blake's girl **Ailly Blake**, whom Courthorne ruined; brother **Larry Blake**, farmer). Shot by Courthorne in Ch. IV; dying words "Witham."
- **Trooper Payne** (English; later Corporal Payne). Trooper **Tom**, **Jake**, **Bacon**, **Hilton**, **Jackson**, **Harland** (magistrate), **Harmon** (whisky runner), **Musquash** (Blackfoot).
- **Sergeant Stimson** (grizzled, keen-eyed, North-West Police).
- **Colonel Barrington** (founder of Silverdale Grange ~10 yrs earlier; autocratic, ex-cavalry, English traditionalist; grey eyes; uncle of Maud; sister Miss Barrington is his sister; Maud is his niece and ward; Lance's kinsman).
- **Miss Barrington** (silver-haired, gentle aunt; knew Witham's mother; had once a lover who died in India beside a mountain gun).
- **Maud Barrington** (Colonel's niece, ~ late 20s/young; brown hair, brown eyes, Montreal-educated; "Princess of the Prairie"; holds Silverdale wheat land in her own right). Friends: **Twoinette** (Montreal), **Evelyn**, **Lily** (girl who kissed Atterly).
- **Gordon Dane** (big bronzed middle-aged bachelor; Colonel's chief lieutenant; "lost money" in speculation earlier; mother-friend of Ferris's mother Ethel Ferris).
- **Graham** (Winnipeg wheat-broker, "Colonel" mockery, later partner in St. Louis mills).
- **Macdonald** (Silverdale farmer, wife Mrs. Macdonald; birch-log house).
- **Ferris** (weak English lad, Silverdale; vindictive; lost to gambler; caused grass fire; expelled).
- **Alfreton** (young Silverdale lad, speculated, saved by Witham).
- **Atterly**, **Carshalton**, **Stapleton** (lad who raced), **Allardyce**, **Allender**, **Hassal**, **Mrs. Carndall**, **Jasper** (Mrs. Jasper, hotel at railroad town), **Broughton** (hotel), **Charley** (hired man), **Tom** & **Jake** (hired men), **Dr.** (doctor at settlement).
- **Witham's cook** (unnamed). **Lawyer** (Winnipeg; Colonel's legal adviser; unnamed).

## Key Plot Events (in order)
1. Ch I: Witham at Canadian settlement, gets two letters (foreclosure; refusal of loan from friend). Nettie gives him no supper. Drives home, team bolts down ravine; horses wrecked; he shoots one (with long knife); other unhurt, he rides home.
2. Ch II: Courthorne visits Witham's cabin. Offers $100 to ride his black horse south along Montana trail as decoy for Stimson's troopers, personating him for a fortnight. Witham agrees (Courthorne lied: "no risk beyond a few days' detention"). Witham notices whip mark on Courthorne's face.
3. Ch III: Shannon and Payne quarrel background (Courthorne whipped Shannon's face after Ailly's ruin). Stimson's plan: Payne watches Montana trail, Shannon watches bluff above Graham's Pool. Witham rides black, Shannon gallops after him at night; Witham escapes over bridge; Witham sings a song.
4. Ch IV: In the bluff, Courthorne holds up Shannon at Marlin rifle point, shoots him (twice). Courthorne flees on tethered horse, Payne pursues; Courthorne rides into river; ice breaks; presumed drowned. Stimson thrown from horse. Shannon dying words: "Witham's horse and his cap... It was... Witham." Rifle found marked "F. Witham."
5. Ch V: Maud Barrington returns from Montreal; Colonel Barrington meets her at railroad town; sleigh ride; Colonel's history of Lance (terrier hanged; gardener's lad; lie). Silverdale Grange; wheat falling.
6. Ch VI: Maud & aunt talk about Lance's history; Maud vows to give him fair trial. Colonel & Dane with Graham: Graham advises selling forward; Colonel refuses.
7. Ch VII: Witham at American outpost; officer tells him Witham "drowned," warrant out. Witham decides to impersonate Courthorne to claim Silverdale inheritance. Lawyer in Annerly offers buyout from Colonel; Witham refuses money, claims land.
8. Ch VIII: Witham arrives at Silverdale levee; meets Miss Barrington (kisses hand), Maud (cold). Whist/poker incident. Dane invites him home; Witham sells wheat against Colonel's wishes.
9. Ch IX: Blizzard; Witham and Maud shelter in half-way shanty (Macdonald's). Witham gives her furs; she sleeps; he walks all night. Next morning he takes her... (Colonel told by Witham; Witham returns to Grange).
10. Ch X: Witham and Colonel; Maud promises Colonel's wheat not sold forward; Witham asks Maud to have all her land sown. Maud gives promise.
11. Ch XI: Witham ploughs with four horses; Miss Barrington blesses "God speed your plough"; Maud asks him to release her promise; he refuses; asks him to handle Ferris (gambler lad). Witham resolves to leave after vindicating.
12. Ch XII: Gambling at railroad hotel saloon; Witham exposes cardsharp; Ferris lost to him. Ferris insults Witham ("She asked you to!"). Witham meets trooper (Ferris? no—English trooper, Alberta Squadron) who suspects.
13. Ch XIII: Ferris gossip at Macdonald's; Maud publicly defends Witham. Drive home in storm of wind/moonlight; Maud says "I shall never believe them."
14. Ch XIV: Witham offers bargain for Maud's unbroken land; Maud pays for ploughing; Courthorne returns (alive) at Witham's farm; demands $1,000; Witham agrees on condition he stay away until harvest. Sergeant Stimson visits.
15. Ch XV: Summer; Maud & Witham talk at mowing. Grass fire lit by someone; Witham leads defence; Ferris set fire (later revealed). Witham injured (kicked), taken to Grange. Dane discovers arson.
16. Ch XVI: Maud nurses; Ferris confronted; Dane and Miss Barrington expel him; Ferris taken to railroad. Witham recovering; Maud asks him not to investigate fire.
17. Ch XVII: Wheat rises; Witham's market deal; Alfreton saved; Graham's supper; Witham asks for bridge funding (~$100 Dane).
18. Ch XVIII: Bridge scene at night; Maud rides up; Courthorne appears, insults Witham, backs horse near gap; Witham saves him. Courthorne says he'll be "back" later.
19. Ch XIX: Courthorne blunders—steals papers from trooper Bacon; flirts with hotel girl at settlement, ejected by "Jake"; Stimson figures Courthorne's crimes. Witham confronts a stranger (Guyler-named) who thought him Courthorne; Witham throws him out. Rumour via Mrs. Carndall of Courthorne-Witham scandal; Miss Barrington doubts.
20. Ch XX: Stimson and Payne at bridge; Payne (now corporal) questions Witham about papers. Dane informed of rumour. Witham and Maud in hall; Courthorne's face at window; Courthorne collapses; Witham takes him away in wagon.
21. Ch XXI: Courthorne sick (pulmonary haemorrhage); confesses; Witham pays $500 to go to Chicago. Witham takes up Colonel's unhedged contract, buys wheat; Colonel gives IOU.
22. Ch XXII: Harvest; Colonel visits wheat field. Stimson arrests whisky-runner Harmon's partner (who sheltered Courthorne/Witham-horse man).
23. Ch XXIII: Harvest finished; Witham decides to confess publicly at harvest feast; Colonel's speech; Courthorne arrives drunk/ill; Witham reveals identity; Courthorne flees; Payne arrives with warrant for Courthorne, who escapes.
24. Ch XXIV: Maud says "The comedy is over... That will make it easier" (Miss Barrington); Witham taken by Stimson. Courthorne flees south; Payne shoots him; Courthorne dies after deposition clearing Witham; Colonel mourns.
25. Ch XXV: Snow; Maud & Witham; Witham refuses to stay; goes to Graham; becomes partner in St. Louis flour mills; $30,000 target.
26. Ch XXVI: A year later; Colonel ill (sleigh overturned, died/failing); Witham returns; proposes to Maud; accepted. Miss Barrington blesses. "There never was a Courthorne who could stand beside him."

## Notable quotes
- Witham: "Pshaw! There's no use kicking against what has to be."
- Courthorne: "Did it ever strike you... that you were not unlike me?"
- Witham (to Maud): "Would you... I'll not be your husband..." (not verbatim).
- Maud: "Lance, my aunt was wiser than I was... What she gave you... was already yours by right."
- Miss Barrington: "Sow in hope, and God speed your plough!"
- Maud: "Yes, we."
- Colonel: "Blood will tell."
